summary.en: Salvadoran special forces have entered Haiti to search for four missing Salvadoran soldiers and four kidnapped aviation technicians after a gang ambush captured them. Haitian gangs carried out the ambush, and remains have been recovered, which President Bukele says are not those of the missing Salvadoran personnel. Displacement continues as civilians flee violence in the communes of Petite Rivière de l'Artibonite and Arcahaie. The conflict produced 193 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Salvadoranske spesialstyrker har gått inn i Haiti for å lete etter fire savnede salvadoranske soldater og fire kidnappede luftfartsteknikere etter at en gjengoverfall fanget dem. Haitiske gjenger utførte overfallet, og levninger er blitt funnet, som president Bukele sier ikke er de savnede salvadoranske personene. Forflytning fortsetter mens sivile flykter fra vold i kommunene Petite Rivière de l'Artibonite og Arcahaie. Konflikten førte til 193 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
